title: When the input unit differs from the limit's unit, the rate limit is enforced after execution instead of as a precondition
content:
The two sUSDe cooldown paths are guarded differently. `cooldownAssetsSUSDe(uint256 usdeAmount)` enforces the limit up front: "The operator must enforce a rate limit on how much sUSDe can be cooled down", `rateLimited(LIMIT_SUSDE_COOLDOWN, usdeAmount)` (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.4.2.3.1.2). `cooldownSharesSUSDe(uint256 susdeAmount)` (.4.2.3.2.1) lists only `onlyRole(RELAYER)` and `isActive` — no `rateLimited` modifier. Instead it decodes "the amount of shares that were actually cooled down (`cooldownAmount`)" (.4.2.3.2.2.1) and then calls `rateLimits.triggerRateLimitDecrease(LIMIT_SUSDE_COOLDOWN, cooldownAmount)` (.4.2.3.2.3).

The reason is unit mismatch. `LIMIT_SUSDE_COOLDOWN` is denominated in assets, but the shares variant is given a share amount whose asset value is only known after the contract converts it. A precheck is impossible without duplicating the vault's conversion logic, so the limit is settled from the return value instead.

Both paths therefore consume the same bucket, but with different guarantees. The assets path cannot exceed the remaining allowance. The shares path can: a single call is executed first and accounted second, so one oversized call can drive the limit to zero or into deficit before anything stops it. The limit constrains the *next* action, not this one.

This is the same check-then-reconcile trade Spark makes on Aave withdrawals, but with the precheck removed entirely rather than merely refined. The design accepts a one-call overshoot as the price of supporting share-denominated actions — a bounded but real hole in what otherwise looks like a hard cap.
description: cooldownAssetsSUSDe carries a rateLimited precheck in asset terms; the share-denominated cooldownSharesSUSDe has no precheck and instead decodes the realized amount and decrements the same limit
